sentences.text: The scientific name of this species is Atrociraptor marshalli.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — contains parts of the skull, lower jaw, teeth, and other fragments. This animal was estimated to be 1.8 to 2 meters long and weighed 15 kg.

As a dromaeosaurid, it likely possessed a large sickle-claw on its second toe and pennaceous feathers. It differed from relatives by having a much deeper face, teeth inclined more strongly backwards, and teeth of nearly uniform size.
Studies suggest dromaeosaurids used their sickle-claws to grasp and restrain prey while dismembering them with their mouths, similar to how modern birds of prey operate.

The genus and species were described by Philip J. Currie and David Varricchio in 2004 after the fossil was found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. The discovery site was approximately 5 km from the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology.

Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2016 that Atrociraptor could attack and wound relatively large prey more effectively than its relatives due to its robust head and dentition. Powers and colleagues noted in 2022 that dromaeosaurids with deep maxillae, like Atrociraptor, were predators characterized by large size, serrated teeth, recurved claws, and a developed sense of smell.

Atrociraptor is classified as a member of the subfamily Eudromaeosauria within the family Dromaeosauridae. A 2009 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and Currie reclassified Atrociraptor into the subfamily Saurornitholestinae alongside Saurornitholestes. Recent updated phylogenetic analyses often consistently place Atrociraptor within the subfamily Saurornitholestinae.

Atrociraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age. The holotype comes from the Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, dating to 72.2–71.5 million years ago. This same member dates from approximately 72.2 to 71.5 million years ago.
Evidence suggests Atrociraptor survived for over 2 million years across a wide geographic area.

Scientists debate the dispersal pattern of Eudromaeosauria, with uncertainty regarding whether the group originated in North America or immigrated from Asia. The internal classification of Eudromaeosauria is uncertain, which complicates determining the exact placement of Atrociraptor within the group. By 2012, there was no scientific consensus on the affinity of Atrociraptor to other dromaeosaurids due to conflicting phylogenetic analyses. It is debated whether Atrociraptor moved elsewhere due to climate change or went extinct, as no remains have been found from the youngest sediments.
